C-PREFS-TRUTH.IntentSummary: Make the preferences pipeline tell the truth end to end across eight coupled defects on the same prefs/theme surface (config-hygiene wave 11 plus frontend F-004/F-011, all re-verified live in the beta-gate-wave worktree on 2026-11-21): the single hydration load point (ASK_FOR_USER_PREFERENCE → SET_USER_PREFERENCE) validates every key documented in _shims/preferences/schema.json against its declared type/enum/range/pattern and repairs an invalid value in memory to its schema default exactly once per key with a loud BLOCK_PREFERENCES_REPAIR marker (F-007), so a hand-edited "autoSave": "false" string can no longer enable write-through autosave through the truthy store/editor.js gate and an autoSaveDelay of 0 can no longer reach setTimeout raw while the General tab renders 1-10 seconds; saving or resetting an empty customCss actually empties style#custom-styles instead of dying on a falsy early return (F-001/F-011); the theme application path stops letting its inline --editorAreaWidth mirror silently revert the saved global editorLineWidth on a tab without a per-document entry, extending the C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES precedence (document > theme > global) to the legacy global tier without forking a second writer (F-002); the documented schema stops contradicting the shipped autosave default (schema autoSave default false → true, pinned to preferenceDefaults() by a consistency test, with zero behaviour change — the C-AUTOSAVE-DEFAULT-ON factory true stays; F-005); tools/dev-smoke.sh dispatches explicitly so a typo'd argument prints usage and exits non-zero before touching the dev server, any process or any build, and --check exits non-zero on a dead server or a missing Mark process instead of always 0 (F-008/F-009); the two Mac App Store recipes converge on one build profile — mas-pkg.sh's hint names tauri.mas.conf.json and the stale mas.conf.json loses its divergent 2.5.0/2.5.1 metadata (keep-or-drop of bundleVersion is owner-review at PR time; F-006); the Appearance tab stops offering the no-op System frame choice on Windows where decorations:false and effectiveTitleBarStyle force custom (F-010); and a pinned per-document theme applies to the document surface only while sidebar, title bar and quick-settings keep following the global mode (frontend F-004), with unpin/tab-switch restoring today's contract.

/// Loose-typed prefs store. Schema validation is the renderer's job

T-001.Title: F-007: schema-driven hydration validation with one-shot in-memory repair and BLOCK_PREFERENCES_REPAIR markers in SET_USER_PREFERENCE

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/renderer/src/store/preferences.js gains a schema-driven validator consulted by the single hydration load point so that SET_USER_PREFERENCE validates exactly the keys documented in src/renderer/src/_shims/preferences/schema.json before they enter the store: a value must satisfy the schema's declared "type", "enum" membership where declared, "minimum"/"maximum" for numbers and "pattern" for strings; a value failing its constraints is repaired IN MEMORY to the schema "default" (or the preferenceDefaults() factory value where the schema entry omits one) exactly once per key during hydration, and each repair emits a loud console marker of the shape [PREFERENCES][BLOCK_PREFERENCES_REPAIR] key=... raw=... reason=type|enum|min|max|pattern naming the key, the offending raw value and the reason. A fully valid profile loads byte-for-byte as today with zero repairs and zero markers; keys outside the documented schema, the session-only experimental keys, and null/undefined values keep today's pass-through untouched (the C-38 T-004 null-guard at :521-525 stays). After repair, both consumers agree on the corrected value: the Settings form (General tab toggle and the autoSaveDelaySeconds range) and the autosave pipeline (store/editor.js :1893 gate reading autoSave, :1937 setTimeout(..., autoSaveDelay)) — a saved "autoSave": "false" string no longer enables write-through autosave and a saved autoSaveDelay of 0/10001/non-number no longer reaches the timer raw.

Conservative scope, per the spec constraint: validation covers ONLY keys the documented schema declares, and documented legacy consumer value forms are NOT "repaired" — concretely codeFontSize stored as the string "14px" (the C-49 contract parsed by util/theme.js addCommonStyle via Number.parseFloat at theme.js :313-316, even though the schema declares type number at schema.json :243-249) passes through unvalidated and unmarked; where the schema and a consumer contract disagree on legacy value forms, the consumer contract wins and the key stays unvalidated until its schema entry is honest. The original preferences file is never rewritten: repair is in-memory at load time and persists only when the user next saves that key through the existing SET_SINGLE_PREFERENCE path, whose write semantics are unchanged; RESET_PREFERENCES_TO_DEFAULTS is unchanged beyond any shared-validator reuse; the backend store keeps m005_prefs.rs load_from semantics (no src-tauri change in this task).

New renderer suite tests/renderer/store/preferences-load-repair.test.js (house-style VERSION + START_MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY markup) covering at minimum: a hand-written but valid profile loads with zero repairs and zero markers; "autoSave": "false" (string) is repaired to true with exactly one marker naming key and reason; autoSaveDelay 0, 10001 and a non-number are each repaired to 5000 with one marker each; codeFontSize "14px" passes through unrepaired and unmarked; an unknown key and a session-only key pass through untouched; and the corrected store value is what the autosave gate and the General-tab presentation read. Store markup synchronized: preferences.js VERSION bump, a dated 2026-11-21 CHANGE_SUMMARY entry naming C-PREFS-TRUTH and the repair boundary, START_BLOCK_/END_BLOCK_ pairs unique and balanced.

T-002.Title: F-001/F-011: addCustomStyle empties the custom layer for real on sheet save and reset

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/renderer/src/util/theme.js addCustomStyle loses the falsy-customCss early return (:340): saving an empty customCss now clears or empties the existing style#custom-styles element (empty its textContent when present; never force-create a fresh empty element when none exists) so the open window immediately returns to the active theme's styles — computed styles on themed elements return to the theme value — and a later non-empty save applies again through the same element. Both paths clear: the sheet save (customCssSheet.vue save :79-81 → SET_SINGLE_PREFERENCE customCss → app.vue watch :266-268 → addCustomStyle, including the cross-window broadcast echo) and the reset path (RESET_PREFERENCES_TO_DEFAULTS through the same watch). Verified for both a light and a dark active theme.

tests/renderer/util/theme.test.js gains the C-PREFS-TRUTH pins without weakening any existing test: after a non-empty apply, an empty save empties the custom-styles layer (textContent empty, computed style back to theme), a subsequent non-empty save applies again, and the empty path is exercised from a truthy-to-falsy store transition exactly as the watch delivers it.

New component test tests/renderer/prefComponents/custom-css-sheet.test.js: the sheet's save with an empty draft produces the customCss preference write that clears the stale layer (store mocked/asserted), and a non-empty draft produces the apply — the component's own template/markup beyond the save path is untouched (the AffectedAreas lists customCssSheet.vue as "save path only if needed"; if no component edit is required the file is unchanged and only the new test lands). House-style markup on the new test file; theme.js VERSION bump plus a dated CHANGE_SUMMARY entry naming C-PREFS-TRUTH.

T-003.Title: F-002: one width precedence across a theme switch — the legacy global tier keeps the saved editorLineWidth effective

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/renderer/src/util/theme.js: after ANY theme application the effective --editorAreaWidth obeys the pipeline precedence per-document entry > global setting > theme/shipped default. Concretely: on a tab with no per-document width entry, a theme switch must not revert the saved global editorLineWidth — the theme stylesheet's re-declared --editorAreaWidth and the inline mirror (:219-233) must not out-rank the legacy global tier that setEditorWidth (:290-296) writes, in both switch orders (theme then width, width then theme); with a per-document entry the pipeline value still wins through reapplyLastEditorWidth (:280) exactly as shipped. The C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES locked model is NOT renegotiated: document > theme > global precedence, the single-writer rule (exactly one owner of the inline --editorAreaWidth at a time), render-time clamping with unmutated stored values, and reapplyLastEditorWidth's pipeline-tier contract stay intact — the fix extends the same precedence to the legacy global tier and forks no second writer; src/renderer/src/util/pageWidth.js semantics stay unchanged (its contract is explicitly out of scope; if a one-line ordering accommodation is unavoidable it must not alter the writer/reset contract and is recorded in the module markup).

New suite tests/renderer/util/theme-width-precedence.test.js: with a global editorLineWidth set and no per-document entry, applying another theme leaves the effective --editorAreaWidth matching the global setting (asserted against the resolved variable, both switch orders); with a recorded pipeline width, the pipeline value wins; and the reapplyLastEditorWidth contract (no-op when nothing recorded) is pinned unchanged. The existing page-width unit suites stay green UNCHANGED (tests/renderer/util/page-width.test.js and tests/renderer/store/editor-page-width.test.js pass with no edits).

theme.js carries a C-PREFS-TRUTH comment at the ordering fix; VERSION bump plus dated CHANGE_SUMMARY entry; no behaviour change to addThemeStyle beyond the width ordering and T-002's addCustomStyle path (the body.dark, color-scheme, syncNativeWindowTheme and CodeMirror skin behaviours stay byte-comparable).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: tools/dev-smoke.sh dispatches explicitly: the full cycle (start_dev_server, build_binary, launch_mark) runs for the no-argument invocation and for an explicit --full (new case arm) only; --quick keeps the quick path; --check runs health-only; ANY unknown argument prints usage via a new print_usage function and exits non-zero BEFORE touching the dev server, any process or any build — no server restart, no cargo build, no kill of a running Mark on the unknown path. --check exits honestly: when the dev server is unreachable (check_dev_server non-200) or the Mark process is absent (pgrep -f "target/debug/mark"), the script exits non-zero; it exits 0 only when both the server answers HTTP 200 and the process is alive. The human-readable health report (green/red lines, the BLOCK_TITLEBAR_TRANSPARENT_OVERLAY_OK presence warning at :98-102) is kept; a C-PREFS-TRUTH comment in the script records the exit contract.

Recorded probes (evidence in the change bundle, run independently against a controlled state): bash -n tools/dev-smoke.sh passes; bash tools/dev-smoke.sh --chekc (typo) prints usage, exits non-zero, and a running sentinel survives untouched (no restart, no build, no kill) — verifiable by a background sentinel process surviving the probe; --check exits 0 with server HTTP 200 and process alive, exits non-zero with a dead server, and exits non-zero with a missing process.
